build: European C64 release, C64 Comics Group T64

exclude: Processor port, transient IRQ saves, renderer and music pointers, and live actor and skater state. The final unpacker starts its game output at $0400.
extra: Address span written by the final unpacker before the jump to $0850

comments.text: Page-aligned lookup used by the retained serial receive routine. Its four indexed OR loads at $0620 through $0632 assemble a byte from separate reads of CIA2 port A.
The nonuniform final 32 bytes of the loader's lookup page, following the 224-byte patterned portion. The serial routine's page reads use unmasked CIA values as indices.
Copy loader code from $0659 to $0330 and from $0600 to $02A7. The routine sets up the IEC commands and drive bootstrap; the game entry at $0850 follows the archive depacker instead.
Push $08 and jump to the copied serial-loader routine at $0330.
Data following the loader trampoline. It contains a fragment of a BASIC loading message, a screen-space fill and a short set of alternating low and high byte values up to the receiver at $0600.
Start of the receiver copied to $02A7. It synchronises its port reads and combines four $0400-page lookups. The following routines implement the fast loader's transfer and bookkeeping.
Source of the code copied to $0330 by $0500. It saves the VIC and CIA state, reads the transfer, stores data through the destination pointer and restores the machine at the end.
The retained byte immediately before the first screen-enable trampoline.
Call the relocated loader, set the VIC display-enable bit and jump to the game start at $0850.
NOP padding after the first copy of the screen-enable trampoline, up to its copy at $0800.
Second copy of the screen-enable trampoline. The 80 bytes at $0800–$084F are identical to $0700–$074F.
Set the shared sprite colours, prepare the high-score title and install the raster interrupt. After port 2 fire, reset the score, credit and ticket state, then enter the city update loop.
Update skater and course state, check the map tile, wait for the raster signal and redraw the sprites and visible terrain. Start the next round when the park count reaches four.
Hide the sprites and put the continue message over the playfield. Count the displayed digit down while waiting for fire. A successful response calls $1140 and increments the used-credit byte.
Draw GAME OVER and MONEY BONUS. Decrement the packed-BCD cash balance one unit at a time and update the score before checking the high-score table.
Eleven custom glyph codes for GAME OVER, including the trailing space. The end-of-session branch copies them to $F4FF.
Thirteen custom glyph codes for MONEY BONUS. Displayed during the cash-to-score conversion.
The first 13-cell line of the continue prompt, PRESS FIRE TO.
The second 13-cell line of the continue prompt, with the word CONTINUE padded for the display.
Set the sound-effect timer to $64, shut off three SID gates, then set voice 1 to a short triangle tone with a fixed high frequency byte.

When the current tile maps to action $10 and the map cooldown is clear, copy the two 20-column halves of the overview into the screen, disable sprites and wait for fire. Returning restores sprite enable and starts the cooldown.
Use the skater's X position relative to $64 and Y relative to $28 and $3C to choose one of six map locations. Stamp an arrow and a marker into that section of the overview.
A retained one-byte return between the map-marker jump and the next coordinate case.
The first 13-cell window into a 14-cell arrow strip. The marker goes at the first cell of the selected destination row.
The second 13-cell window into the same arrow strip. The marker goes at column 12 of the selected destination row.
Copy the arrow strip from $0B82 and put the marker in the final column of this position group.
Shift and rotate the two raster-seeded state bytes at $3EBD–$3EBE, combine them with XOR and ADC, and save the result in the low state byte.
Read the low raster byte into $3EBD and its doubled value into $3EBE, retrying while the doubled byte is zero.
Walk the ranked score pairs from the bottom. Shift displaced scores and their eight-character names down, then call the joystick name-entry screen at the insertion point.
Install the name-entry raster callback and draw eight input cells. Left and right rotate the character strip. Fire accepts the selected glyph, backs up at $F5 or ends the name at $F6.
Custom character indices for the NEW HIGH SCORE text in the new high score display.
Custom character indices for the ENTER YOUR NAME text in the enter name display.
Enable only sprite zero, place it at $B0,$74 and assign sprite pointer $B9 and colour 1 for name entry.
Draw 40 cells from the circular 32-glyph name-entry alphabet, starting at the current selection. The displayed selection is read back from $F57C.
Circular 32-entry glyph strip for joystick name entry. The control glyphs $F5 and $F6 act as backspace and finish when selected.

Silence the three voices, draw the title and rank table, and copy the credit strings into the screen. Wait for port 2 fire to be released and pressed again, then set up play colour RAM and the raster interrupt.
Thirty-three custom glyph codes for the U.S. Gold copyright line on the title.
Thirty-three custom glyph codes for the Atari Games copyright line on the title.
Thirty-three custom glyph codes containing the Chris Butler credit and its padding.
Five bytes between the title-credit glyph block and the logo setup. The three credit loops end at $0EC9.
Set up four expanded monochrome sprites. Pairs share coordinates and combine yellow and red layers of the title logo using pointers $BA–$BD.
Clear the display, then draw the rank, eight-character name and six-digit score for each of seven entries in the forty-column screen.
Scale X by four to find the rank's four glyphs and draw them with colour 3.
Scale X by eight to find the rank's saved name and draw it in colour 1.
Use X to select a two-byte packed-BCD score, render its four nibbles as digits, then append two zeros.
Four glyph slots per displayed rank. The rank routine plots the slots in order, with the fourth providing spacing.
Eight mutable custom glyph codes per ranked name. The handover table seeds the first name with A characters.
The next six eight-glyph name records, seeded with repeated B to G characters. Insertion moves eight bytes per downward shift.
Seven two-byte packed-BCD scores, high then low. The title adds two fixed zeros after each converted pair.
Low packed-BCD byte of the first score at $106E. The score insertion code compares this half when the high values match.
High byte of the second ranked score, also the start of the destination range for shifting earlier rows down.
Low byte of the second rank, followed by the high and low pairs for the lower ranks.
Fill the forty-column display area with the blank character before drawing another screen.
Set the skater and saved position to column $5F, row $38, with the opening viewport 20 cells to the left and 10 cells above.
Mark the sixteen actor Y positions outside the city, then run the class-specific actor setup routines for the current difficulty.
Write four map tile IDs $D8–$DB as a two-by-two square at the caller's row and column pointer.
Write two blank tiles over a pair of edge tiles in the completed park's entrance.
Increase the city difficulty counter to at most nine, load its actor-update pointer, reset the per-shop visit flags and rebuild scenery and actor data before returning to play.
Rebuild the status panel, reset the city timer and motion and crash state, then select sprite modes and palette for the layered skater.
Eleven little-endian stage dispatch words. City actor updates jump through the word chosen by $1111.
High byte of the first actor handler word. The stage setup reads both halves from the interleaved pointer table at $11C9.
Draw the twelve-cell PARK TIMER caption and B, S and G marks used by the timer-based courses.
Custom character indices for the PARK TIMER text in the park timer display.
Draw the twelve-cell MEDAL METER caption and the B, S and G marks for the manoeuvre-based courses.
Custom character indices for the MEDAL METER text in the medal meter display.
Reapply the open-entrance tile patterns at all four park entrances. Replace the four grade marker glyphs with the digit for the new round.
Stamp the six four-character rows at $1311 into the caller's map coordinates. The map row stride is 256 bytes.
Six by four tile diagram for the open form of the first class of park entrance. Rows step 256 bytes in the world map.
Stamp the six rows at $1340 after a gauge-based event. Each row occupies four adjacent map cells.
Used form of the entrance diagram stamped by $1329, six rows of four terrain tile IDs.
Stamp the six rows at $136F into the city at the supplied map pointer.
Second open-entrance design, copied as six four-cell rows by $1358.
Stamp the six rows at $139E when the clock-based park has been used.
Second used-entrance design, used by the two clock-and-stunt parks when the skater returns.
Set the four city-map destinations for the shop signs and regenerate their displayed cash prices.
Draw the two rows of text for the remaining clock-course bonus, clearing the rows around the message.
Custom character indices for the BONUS FOR text in the trick bonus header display.
Custom character indices for the MANOEUVERS text in the trick bonus amount display.
Draw the two sixteen-cell lines for the remaining gauge bonus and clear the cells above and below them.
Custom character indices for the BONUS FOR text in the timed bonus header display.
Custom character indices for the REMAINING TIME text in the timed bonus amount display.
Wait for the raster counter between steps, draining one bar unit and adding one score unit each time. Wait again after the bar is empty.
Clear the two-row price sign area, set its currency symbol and fall through to write the round price digits.
Read the current round's price pair at $1C87 and draw its three decimal digits through the caller's pointer.
Place a two-row, six-column open-park pattern from $14CE and $14D4 in the city tile map.
Six tile IDs for the upper row of the open park sign.
The lower six open-sign tiles, copied one world row below $14CE's destination.
Place the two six-cell rows at $14F2 and $14F8 over a used park's sign.
Six replacement tiles for the upper sign row after a park visit.
Six lower-row tiles for the used park sign.
Convert the packed-BCD threshold pair at the index in $3EA8 into the first three glyphs of the next-ticket score on the panel.
Two packed-BCD bytes per ticket threshold in low-then-high order. The panel adds two trailing zero glyphs.
First high byte of the interleaved milestone table. The award condition compares these high bytes for equality before testing the low byte.
Add A to the four-digit decimal score. Compare against the current two-byte ticket threshold and advance the threshold when met, while capping held tickets at four.
Turn the four packed-BCD score nibbles into custom font codes at $F6FF–$F702.
On selected raster-counter values, reduce the current city timer. On expiry switch to the warning message, seed the pursuing actor at a viewport edge and flash the warning colours.
Custom character indices for the SKATE OR DIE text in the skate or die display.
Clamp the gauge to $4F. Fill full cells with glyph $A8, draw the partial cell with $EC and replace the eight bytes of glyph $EC with the selected bit pattern.
Four one-byte patterns used to rewrite all eight lines of glyph $EC to show the timer's partially filled cell.
If the crash and end flags permit an impact, use the pads upgrade to set recovery time, set speed to $40, trigger the impact sound and choose a direction from the vertical component.
Delay values indexed by pads upgrade count. Used both after actor contact and after a landing with excessive facing error.
Count down the tile-score overlay. On expiry restore the three saved tile codes at the original map pointer.
Add one point per four counted turning steps to the terrain bonus, clamp the result to nine and store it for the score update.
For a positive result, save three original map cells and put a temporary number and zeros into those cells. Copy the old collision actions onto the new glyphs and set the restoration delay to $32.
At difficulty three or above, initialise actor slots zero to two along row $52 with their starting sprites, colours and steering state.
At difficulty two or above, initialise slots 13 and 14 at row $17 with the frames $C6 and $C7 used by their position-jitter routine.
At difficulty two or above, seed the actor in slot 15 and three more actors at their roaming start positions, with directions and sprite flags.
Initialise actor slots 11 and 12 around the middle of the map, at rows $2D and $3A, ready to move around their shared rectangle.
Seed slot six unless the difficulty is zero. At difficulty two or higher also seed slot seven.
Set sprite $B8 and colour 6 for the chasing actor and move its starting Y outside the active viewport.
At nonzero city difficulty, seed one actor in slot nine. Give slot ten its on-map Y at difficulty two or higher.

For early city difficulty, initialise two groups of three adjacent actor slots near the opposite ends of one street. Give the groups their component sprite IDs, positions, colours and expansion flags.
Stamp six rows from $1AAD at successive positions starting at $A998. Make the separate sixteen-tile strip at $66EF a finish line by filling it with $CC.
Six rows of six course tile codes. Their destination advances by $0102 per row, and $1A74 writes the finish tile across a separate sixteen-cell strip.
Stamp six rows from $1B0A at the same map positions later used by $1A74 and reset the finish strip at $66EF to tile $01.
Six rows of six tile codes used by $1AD1 before the final course segment. Each following row moves two map columns to the right.
Convert A from binary to three decimal digits by repeated doubling and subtraction. Place the glyphs next to the ticket heading at $F79A and write their colour cells.

On tile $F1, choose the shop from world coordinates. A clear visit flag permits a debit attempt. If cash suffices and the level is below nine, increment both level and visit flag. At level nine a successful debit leaves both bytes alone.
Restore the previous world position, clear speed and draw the equipment-shop refusal message and its cash heading.
Custom character indices for the NO SALE text in the no sale display.
Custom character indices for the YOU NEED MORE MONEY text in the insufficient cash display.
Draw the item name, cost label and purchase price in the shop popup. The preceding call to $2E61 writes upgrade levels to the city status panel.
Custom character indices for the HOT text in the purchase prefix display.
Custom character indices for the COST text in the purchase cost display.
Four little-endian pointers for the six-character equipment words that follow, in the same order as the upgrade counters.
High operand of the first equipment label pointer. The four short name records after the pointer table are helmet, shoes, board and pads.
Ten round-indexed prices, with the high packed-BCD byte before the low.
Low byte of the first round's price. The price signage and cash deduction use the same interleaved table.
Tile $CA triggers the park checks. A ticket is required, then X and Y bands select one of the four park entry routines.
Restore the position saved before movement, clear speed and redraw the no-ticket message before stalling on raster ticks.
Custom character indices for the YOU NEED A TICKET text in the need ticket display.
Spend one ticket and place the skater in the jump course. Rebase the viewport and skater at each course section boundary. Stop on finish tile $CC or when the separate packed-BCD clock reaches zero.
Update skating and the trick-based medal gauge while ticking the separate clock. Move to the next section when the vertical viewport origin reaches $6C.
Initial packed-BCD clock values for the jump course, indexed by the city difficulty counter.
Branch to the medal and cash display for a nonzero result code. Otherwise clear the surrounding text and show the no-medal message.
Custom character indices for the YOU FAILED TO QUALIFY text in the no qualifying medal display.
Look up the medal name and per-round BCD award, multiply by round index plus one, add the result to the balance and display the award in the result overlay.
Three base cash awards in packed BCD, one for each medal tier. The result overlay adds the selected entry once per round.
Custom character indices for the MEDAL text in the medal result heading display.
Custom character indices for the CASH PRIZE text in the cash prize heading display.
Four little-endian addresses indexed by the numeric result code. The selected address points to a six-cell medal name.
High byte of the first name pointer. The interleaved directory is followed by the six-glyph bronze, silver and gold names.
Spend one ticket and place the skater in the downhill course. Rebase the scrolling position at its section boundaries. The finish tile $CC or an empty timer ends play.
Ten round-indexed starting values for the downhill timer bar.
Use a mask supplied by the course loop to gate the meter's decrement. Redraw or classify the meter for the current medal as the gauge falls.
Add the pending award to the gauge, then select its indicator colour and medal tier by thresholds $10, $28 and $40.
Spend a ticket and reset finish state at the left-side course. Update movement and the gauge, call the gate test and show the result when the gauge runs out or finish tile $CC is crossed.
Ten round-indexed starting values for the slalom timer bar.
When the low six bits of the raster counter are zero, subtract one BCD unit from the park clock. Draw its tens and units in the status panel.
Spend a ticket and place the skater in the upper-left ramp course. Update ramp drops, movement, the viewport and the BCD clock until time expires.
Ten packed-BCD time allowances indexed by round for the ramp course.

Save the last ordinary ground position as a recovery point. On tile action $11, run a vertical fall with signed velocity and redraw while falling, then restore the saved coordinates and apply the landing or crash path.
Four four-byte rows between the ramp drop loop and its steering routine. Each row contains three copies of $CE or $50 and ends with zero. Their consumer is open.
Decode the held direction into the current air-facing index, increment the turn count when it changes and choose a ramp sprite pair from the approached face.
On tile $D3, check 25 nearby offsets for $D1 gate tiles. Replace matching tiles with $D2 and add two gauge units per replacement.
25 signed column displacements from the skater's position in the gate-scoring search.
25 signed row displacements paired with the column offsets at $24DC.
Scan the affected rectangle beginning at $9700. Change used gate tile $D2 back to unscored tile $D1 before a run.
Clear the actor's visibility byte and continue the sprite-assignment loop with the preceding actor.
Cull the 16 actor records against the viewport, then project visible actor coordinates to VIC pixels and fill descending sprite slots with their pointers, colours and expansion flags.
One AND mask per VIC sprite slot, each clearing its height-expansion bit.
One OR mask per VIC sprite slot, used when assigning a projected actor X above 255.
Indirect jump through the stage-specific actor handler selected at $1111.
Update the two three-sprite vehicles when their visibility flags are set, run the chasing actor and update the two additional roaming actors when visible.
Keep the two vehicles, add the first cycling obstacle and the marker-route actor, and keep the chaser and two roaming actors.
Replace the early vehicles with individually routed actors and add a second obstacle, the paired marker-route actors and the two top-edge hazards.
Run the third-stage actor set and also animate actor slot two and test skater contact with slots zero and one.
If actor X was visible, compare its tile coordinates to the grounded skater's collision box and call the crash routine on overlap.
Animate the visible group at its X endpoints $8F and $A2, changing two display frames at each endpoint, then integrate its fractional motion.
Periodically change a visible hazard's Y between rows $17 and $16 using the raster-seeded random generator. Check grounded contact separately.
When the city time-out flag is set, move one actor toward the skater in both axes. Increase its speed on selected raster ticks and end the run after a position overlap.
During its initial countdown, use the high state bits to select frames. After that state decays below four, move along the marker route.
Four sprite pointers used both for the marker actor's reaction animation and its movement directions.
Switch direction at the route's four fixed coordinate bounds and integrate the selected component velocities. Nearby skater contact sets up the actor's reaction.
Cycle the obstacle's sprite while visible. An overlap replaces it with sprite $B7 and either crashes a grounded skater or awards six score units to an airborne one.
Four sprite pointers indexed by the visible contact hazard's animation phase.
Use four coordinate limits to choose a new direction, update the actor's two fractional coordinates with table vectors, and test contact with the grounded skater.
Four signed fractional X increments for the later roaming actors.
Four signed fractional Y increments paired with $2AD0.
Four display pointers for the different route directions of later roaming actors.

Change route and three sprite IDs at its map limits. Update the vehicle centre with signed fractional displacement, derive the two side slots and check for a grounded skater in its collision rectangle.
Four signed fractional X increments for the early vehicles and the marker-route actor.
Four signed fractional Y increments paired with $2BF5.

Patrol a rectangle and choose a sprite using raster-counter bit 4. Actor Y one to three tiles below the ground row and actor X at the skater column or one tile to its right can call $16AA while grounded. That routine checks the existing crash and end flags.
Four signed fractional column increments for the two actors that patrol the middle of the map.
Four signed fractional row increments for the middle patrol.
Sprite base frame for each of the middle patrol's four travel directions.
Read the CIA1 matrix. One input toggles the music gate on a fresh press, while a second shows the pause message and waits for another press and release to resume.
Custom character indices for the PAUSED text in the pause message display.
Call the raster-counter wait at $39F0, decrement X and repeat until X is zero. Entry with nonzero X waits X times. Zero wraps and waits 256 times.
Clear 199 cells from $F6F8 through $F7BE, covering rows 19–23 except the final cell. Draw the score, cash, tickets and next-ticket labels and their values and equipment levels.
Custom character indices for the SCORE 000000 text in the score readout display.
Custom character indices for the CASH text in the cash readout display.
Custom character indices for the TICKETS text in the tickets readout display.
Custom character indices for the NEXT TICKET AT 000000 text in the next ticket readout display.
Custom character indices for the TIMER text in the city timer display.
Erase up to four ticket slots, then draw one ticket glyph per held ticket in alternating cells.
Subtract the round-indexed packed-BCD cost from the two-byte cash balance. Return $FF on borrow without changing either balance byte.
Split the two packed-BCD cash bytes into four custom glyph codes for the city panel.
Put the four current upgrade values next to their panel icons.
On water action $0B, switch to the two splash sprites and run a sound and delay. When the delay ends, restore the saved ground position, facing sprites and normal movement flags.
Restore the skater's sprite mode, facing sprites and saved position, and clear movement and crash state after the water delay.
Recognise ramp action $0A, enable the separate shadow sprite, reset the trick counters and search forward for a tile beyond the ramp surface.
Take the shorter distance between the ground facing and the aerial facing around eight directions. If it exceeds the helmet level, start the crash delay and sound.
Decode a nonneutral stick direction into an airborne sprite pair. Increment the turning count on a change of facing.
Convert the port 2 direction nibble into the base sprite pointer for an aerial direction. The second skater layer uses the next sprite.
Convert the port 2 direction nibble into one of eight facing indices.
Apply the friction step only when the raster-counter low nibble is zero.
Move signed speed one step toward zero, preserving a stopped skater.

The facing selects a sprite that the current pose must match to start the push animation on a $3F counter boundary. The separate acceleration test masks the incremented counter with $0F. At sufficient positive speed it uses the board cap, and otherwise it sets speed to $40.
Ten speed ceilings addressed by the board upgrade count.
While the push-animation countdown is nonzero, decrement it and use the current facing to choose the two push sprites.
Two sprite pointers per ground facing for the push animation.
The overlay sprite pointer of the first facing pair. The two-byte stride gives the remaining orientations.
Convert the explicit map coordinates at $2D–$2E to a pointer in the map at $4000 and read the tile ID.
Use the skater's X and ground row to form a pointer into the $4000 tile map and save the resulting tile code.
A fresh fire press saves the takeoff heading and computes vertical velocity from the current movement and the shoes level. The held-fire and released-fire paths continue to steer.
Ten offsets indexed by the shoes upgrade level. The jump poll subtracts the chosen offset from its initial vertical velocity.
Mask the active-low port 2 direction nybble and map the eight cardinal and diagonal bit combinations to facings 0–7.
Distinguish jump, grounded and crash states. Integrate vertical velocity while airborne, recognise landing against the ground row and apply trick scoring or impact recovery before movement resumes.
Eight SID frequency high bytes indexed by the crash countdown while the effect is active.
Decode steering, select animation and horizontal and vertical grade tables from the current tile action, then apply signed fractional movement. Recompute collision and viewport state afterwards.
Mask the priority bit out of the current tile action. Wall action $09 or an impassable ramp edge restores the previous position and reverses the speed.
Restore the saved pre-movement fractions and tile coordinates, set a speed opposite the prior sign and clear the last direction.
Little-endian pointers to eight-direction signed Y factors for terrain action types.
High byte of the first Y movement table pointer. It shares the interleaved directory at $33CE.
One little-endian address per terrain action for its directional speed changes.
High byte of the first directional acceleration-table pointer, followed by the remaining terrain pairs.
One little-endian pointer to facing sprite pairs per terrain action type.
The high byte of the first pose table pointer. The terrain dispatcher advances this table in two-byte steps.
Eight signed X movement factors around the skater's possible headings. The motion code multiplies them by the current speed component.
The ordinary Y row read through $33CE is followed by a zero row for ordinary acceleration at $344A. Later Y and acceleration rows are also interleaved in eight-byte directional groups.
Two sprite IDs per facing, for the ordinary standing and rolling poses.
Terrain-specific lists of two sprite IDs per facing. The directory at $3416 selects the relevant sixteen-byte list for each terrain action.
Eight sprite pairs chosen for the first ramp-face action while the skater is falling through that terrain.
Eight sprite pairs chosen for the other facing of the ramp-side graphics during the drop routine.

A 256-entry table indexed by the ground tile ID. The low seven bits select movement and collision behaviour and bit 7 controls skater sprite priority. Temporary score-glyph entries may be patched to match the terrain concealed underneath them.
The action-table slot for score overlay glyph $9E. The overlay writer substitutes the collision behaviour of the tile it covers.
The action-table slot for overlay glyph $F4. It inherits the terrain action of the original third map cell.
Multiply the magnitudes of the two signed bytes at $26 and $27 by eight shift-and-add steps. Return the signed low product in A.

Keep the skater between left and right horizontal margins and upper and lower vertical margins, subject to the course's viewport limits. Update the fractional scroll values alongside the coarse origin.
Subtract the viewport coordinates and fractions from the skater's world coordinates. Convert the differences to VIC pixels, writing a separate Y value for the shadow sprite.
Low three bits for assigning the layered skater sprites' ninth horizontal coordinate bit.
Set black background and border with multicolour values $0B and $08. Fill 1000 colour RAM cells in 25 rows of 40 with $0E.
Patch the 19 indexed load operands with the viewport's map origin. Each loop copies 40 tile IDs into one row of the display and advances the source by 256 cells.
Low source operand for viewport row 0. The renderer patches it with the coarse map column before writing 40 cells from $F400.
High byte of the source map address for viewport row 0. Its loop copies 40 glyphs to $F400.
